title: No es lo mismo... que: distinciones conceptuales

sections.content: No es lo mismo X que Y (X is not the same thing as Y) is the natural way to draw a sharp conceptual line -- exactly what a definition of "revolution" needs when the everyday and the technical sense of the word get blurred together. These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: No es lo mismo un simple cambio de gobernante que una revolución.
items.english: A simple change of ruler is not the same thing as a revolution.

items.spanish: No es lo mismo derrocar a un presidente que transformar por completo la estructura social de un país.
items.english: Overthrowing a president is not the same thing as completely transforming a country's social structure.

items.spanish: Esta distinción entre revolución política y revolución social resulta fundamental.
items.english: This distinction between political revolution and social revolution turns out to be fundamental.

items.spanish: No es lo mismo un nuevo presidente que un nuevo país.
items.english: A new president is not the same thing as a new country.

sections.content: Both halves of no es lo mismo X que Y can be a noun, an infinitive, or a whole clause -- as long as the two things being contrasted are grammatically parallel, as in derrocar a un presidente (infinitive) que transformar la estructura social (infinitive).
